result:
Sign-up now follows ADR 0003 on all five reports; the existing suite (617 tests) and the type check pass, and a throwaway end-to-end run of the service confirmed the cases below.

- **Names:** "Admin" gets the slug `admin-2`, "Taskflow" gets `taskflow-2`, "Al" gets `al`, and "J" or "山田" fall back to `workspace` (suffixed when taken).
- **Email case:** addresses are stored lowercased and looked up case-insensitively in the user repository, so every caller is covered.
- **Throttling:** sign-up is charged once on the anonymous `auth:register` bucket before anything is written. Throttled sign-up, sign-in and reset confirmation now come back as `rate_limited` (429).
- **Existing address:** refused as `conflict`, nothing created — the ADR overrides the product note's silent success.
- **Long names:** the display name is shortened so the workspace name fits the 64-character limit and still ends in `'s workspace`.

Things I changed that you might not expect:

- **Rate-limit charging moved out of the actions.** The login and password-reset actions used to charge the limiter a second time on top of the service; I removed the action-level charge so each attempt costs one token.
- **Anonymous bucket owner unified.** The service and the actions used different anonymous ids (zeros vs. empty string); both now use the empty-string one.
- **Throttled reset request is now silent on the action path too.** Before, the action surfaced the refusal; the ADR says that endpoint must reveal nothing.
- **`RateLimitedError` lives in a new `src/lib/rate-limit-error.ts`.** The action-errors module re-exports it, so the comment and invite limits now also map to `rate_limited`.

Not fixed: existing duplicate accounts that differ only by case are not merged; lookups return the oldest one. Merging them needs a data migration.
